The musical considers whether family is determined by blood, choice, or the care people learn to give one another. It also weighs youthful uncertainty against the loneliness beneath perpetual freedom, finding warmth and humour in two flawed people learning to face reality together.

show: Mil guitarras - El Rock Musical (musical staged at Espacio Alma, Madrid)
synopsis:
Bear spends his days amid engines, grease and tools in a car workshop, far from the years when he was known as part of Los Bears. Yet the band’s successes between 2005 and 2010 still echo in his mind, along with the conviction that rock once gave shape to every ambition, friendship and dream he had. His routine is interrupted when Rachel, Los Bears’ magnetic former singer, re-enters his life after a minor accident. Her sudden return rekindles the possibility that the music—and the life—they abandoned might not be over after all.

With the old spark revived, Bear and Rachel set out to bring the group back together and reclaim the exhilaration of the stage. Their search does not produce a conventional reunion. Instead, the emerging line-up becomes an unlikely collision of musical worlds: a rapper with formidable flow, Manrico—the workshop friend whose enthusiasm exceeds his judgement—and a dancer whose instincts belong to the world of pop stardom. What begins as an attempt to recover the past turns into a chaotic experiment in finding a new sound and a new way of belonging together.

As rehearsals, memories and clashing personalities push the would-be band forward, Bear must face the distance between the person he was in Los Bears and the man he has become. Rachel’s return makes the past impossible to ignore, but the group’s strange new chemistry also demands that they look beyond nostalgia. Their effort to perform again becomes a wager on whether old dreams can survive adulthood—and whether a second chance has to resemble the first.

The musical celebrates rock as a shared language of memory, rebellion and enduring desire. It also centres on friendship, reinvention and the courage to pursue a dream after life appears to have moved on.

show: Osky y su Hilo Multicolor (musical staged at Teatro Salesianos Estrecho, Madrid)
synopsis:
Torna’s world changes when she meets Osky, a magical being whose light, humour, and wisdom seem to arrive precisely when she needs them most. Their encounter reveals the possibility of an invisible Hilo Multicolor: a thread that joins people who are meant to become friends and remain connected, even when life carries them in different directions. Drawn into a realm where imagination has no boundaries, Torna discovers that dreams can take shape and that every new meeting may alter a person’s life.

As Torna and Osky travel together, music accompanies their discoveries and turns their journey into a succession of heartfelt lessons. They learn that friendship is not earned through popularity, outward appearances, or the approval of others. Instead, it grows from sincerity, empathy, courage, and the freedom to be oneself. Osky encourages Torna to recognise the bonds that matter most: those formed when people offer one another kindness without conditions and choose to see beyond what is visible on the surface.

Yet the adventure also confronts the pain of parting. Torna and Osky must understand that a farewell does not necessarily destroy a true connection. Love, shared memories, and the mark left by a genuine friend continue to shine, like the many colours of a thread that cannot be broken. What begins as an extraordinary encounter becomes an emotional awakening: Torna comes to appreciate that the people she loves may remain beside her in spirit, even when they are no longer physically near.

The musical celebrates friendship as a lasting, heartfelt bond, stronger than appearances, distance, or loss. It also affirms imagination, self-acceptance, and the sustaining power of love and memory.

show: Princesas (musical staged at Teatro Corfú 7, Alicante)
synopsis:
Songs begin to ring out as a procession of princesses enters a world of castles, colour and storybook magic. One by one, they step forward to share episodes from their own adventures, filling the stage with familiar melodies and moments of wonder. Their tales unfold not as a single quest with one heroine, but as a festive journey through several enchanted worlds, where each princess brings a different voice, challenge and dream.

As the stories move from one royal realm to another, the princesses confront the doubts and obstacles that test them: moments that demand courage, acts of kindness, trust in friends and the willingness to believe in themselves. Music turns each encounter into a shared celebration, inviting the young audience to enter the fantasy rather than merely watch it from afar. Castles and splendid costumes may surround the heroines, but their greatest discoveries come from within: they learn that strength is not limited to grand gestures, that friendship can guide them through uncertainty, and that hope can transform even the most daunting moment.

The separate adventures gradually join into an exuberant communal finale. The princesses sing, celebrate and encourage everyone around them to recognise the magic already present in their own hearts. What begins as a passage through tales and songs becomes an active, family-centred celebration in which imagination opens the door to courage, joy and possibility.

The show centres on bravery, friendship, kindness, hope and self-confidence. Its central idea is that true magic does not depend on a castle or a crown, but on believing in oneself and caring for others.

show: Rincones, con Lorena Gómez - Un musical sobre los amores de tu vida (musical staged at Pequeño Teatro Gran Vía, Madrid)
synopsis:
A single performer, a piano and a voice. Macorina stands amid the boxes of a move, determined to impose order on a life that has become too crowded with memories. As she sorts, packs, and decides what deserves a place in the truck, she clings to one apparently simple conclusion: love only gets in the way. Yet each box she opens releases another corner of her past—a face, a feeling, a song, a wound that has not fully closed—and the practical work of changing homes becomes an intimate excavation of everything she thought she had left behind.

Moving through the people who have crossed her path, Macorina revisits the loves that shaped her, unsettled her, delighted her, and taught her to protect herself. Her recollections do not form a neat romantic history. They bring back tenderness and laughter alongside disappointment, longing, doubt, and the uncomfortable awareness that relationships can change the way a person sees herself. Determined to keep love outside her new beginning, she tries to reduce it to excess baggage: something too heavy, too complicated, and too painful to carry any farther.

But the more Macorina attempts to put her past away, the clearer it becomes that it cannot simply be sealed inside a cardboard box. The songs and memories draw her into a candid reckoning with the choices she has made and the emotional traces left by those who mattered to her. What began as an attempt to reorganise a home turns into a confrontation with her own heart: why did she decide that love was an obstacle, and what would it mean to make room for it again?

At its core, the musical considers love as both a source of vulnerability and an inescapable part of identity. It suggests that even when people try to travel light, the loves that have marked them find a way into the luggage.

show: Rita Lee, uma autobiografia musical (musical staged at Teatro Porto Seguro, São Paulo, Brazilian Portuguese-language production)
synopsis:
Rita appears before an audience with the mischief and candour of someone determined to tell her own story without polishing away its messier edges. From the strange fascinations of her childhood and her first glimpses of a life beyond convention, she moves into São Paulo’s feverish musical scene, where a rebellious young artist begins to find a voice that refuses to behave. Music becomes both her refuge and her weapon as she joins Arnaldo Baptista and Sérgio Dias in Os Mutantes, plunging into experimentation, celebrity, conflict and the restless search for artistic freedom.

As the years race forward, Rita recounts the breakups, transformations and excesses that accompany her passage from Os Mutantes to Tutti-Frutti and then to an increasingly self-defined career. Her humour turns sharp when authority, expectation and the machinery of fame try to contain her. Under the dictatorship, an encounter with Censora Solange brings the absurd violence of censorship into view, while Rita’s 1976 imprisonment exposes the personal cost of refusing to be quiet. Yet humiliation, fear and failure never end the story; each setback becomes material for another song, another provocation and another reinvention.

Along the way, the people around Rita enter and leave her world in a parade of affection, rivalry, admiration and irreverence. Elis Regina, Gal Costa, Gilberto Gil, Raul Seixas, Ney Matogrosso and Hebe Camargo appear as figures in the wider constellation of Brazilian music and television, while Charles Lee embodies her family history. Above all, Roberto de Carvalho arrives as Rita’s artistic counterpart and great love: together they forge a partnership that reshapes her sound and sustains her through the contradictions of fame, domestic life and creative ambition. As Rita continues to sing, joke, rage and confess, she also embraces activism for animal rights and faces the ordinary vulnerabilities behind an extraordinary public persona.

The musical celebrates creative freedom, defiance and the right to remain unapologetically oneself. It also treats love, survival, ageing, loss and reinvention as inseparable movements in Rita’s lifelong refusal to be silenced.

show: Rocío Dúrcal es inolvidable (musical staged at Teatre Talia, Valencia)
synopsis:
Carmen Morales enters the theatre carrying a firm refusal: she has been asked to take part in a musical that revisits the life and best-known songs of her mother, Rocío Dúrcal, but twenty years after Rocío’s death, Carmen is unwilling to reopen memories that still hurt. Above all, she believes that her mother is irreplaceable—and that no performance can truly contain a life so vivid, demanding, and beloved.

The project’s author and director, alarmed by Carmen’s answer, persuades her to read the script with him before rejecting it for good. He gives her complete freedom to cut scenes, rewrite passages, add what is missing, or remove anything she cannot bear to face. Over ninety minutes without an interval, the two of them travel through decades of private recollection and public history, interrupting argument and confession with songs, sung live, that summon Rocío’s presence back into the room.

As the rehearsal unfolds, Carmen and the director revisit affectionate, comic, and painful episodes involving Rocío Dúrcal, her father, and Carmen herself. Family anecdotes collide with the pressures of fame, professional sacrifice, new challenges, failures, and triumphs. Their personal memories are interwoven with a Spain undergoing profound change, so that the musical’s imagined past becomes both an intimate family album and a portrait of a country in transformation. With the allotted time steadily running out, Carmen must decide whether she can move beyond grief, accept the role, and allow the musical to open.

The show turns remembrance into a negotiation between a daughter’s need to protect the past and the theatre’s wish to share it. It is about love, loss, artistic inheritance, and the uneasy possibility that singing old songs can make absence feel briefly present.

show: Villanas (musical staged at Teatro Arlequín Gran Vía, Madrid)
synopsis:
In the Limbo de las Villanas, Maléfica, Úrsula, la Reina Malvada and the Madrastra de Cenicienta serve a sentence for the wicked deeds that made them infamous. Their confinement seems endless—until they learn that the Hermandad de las Hadas Madrinas de la Misericordia will grant one villain a pardon, an opportunity offered only once every hundred years. The prospect of freedom turns their shared prison into a contest: only one of them may leave the Limbo, and each must persuade the unseen arbiters that she deserves clemency.

Maléfica, Úrsula, la Reina Malvada and the Madrastra de Cenicienta take turns reclaiming the narrative that condemned them. Through songs, comic confrontations and increasingly competitive revelations, they present the version of events that was never allowed into the stories: their own. Each woman argues that her reputation as a monster has concealed disappointments, grievances, ambitions and injuries that complicate the familiar tale. The four rivals challenge the moral certainty of the heroes who defeated them, question the fairness of their punishment, and turn their rival claims for sympathy into a battle of wit and spectacle.

As the contest advances, the villains must decide whether their escape depends on outdoing one another or on exposing the rules that have kept them trapped in a single, simplified identity. Their competing performances transform the Limbo into a tribunal, concert stage and comic arena, where no account of good and evil remains entirely secure.

The musical examines who gets to tell a story and how easily women branded “villains” can be reduced to caricatures. It pairs parody and humour with questions of judgment, redemption, rivalry and the possibility of being heard on one’s own terms.

show: 快乐即逝 (musical staged at Shanghai Culture Square, Shanghai, Chinese-language production)
synopsis:
The work routine of a grey, monotonous industrial town is broken open when a travelling company arrives with a full-scale musical show — booked by the mayor, who also owns the only factory in the place. His son Joan is days away from marrying Lina, but he is immediately drawn to Zaira, the company’s star. In her he sees the freedom, passion and self-determination he has never been allowed to possess; in him, she recognises a longing for belonging and tenderness beneath the town’s harsh surface.

What follows is built on an exact reversal. Joan wants to run away with Zaira, far from the grey town and the future laid out for him. Zaira wants the opposite: worn out by a life permanently on the road, what she longs for is to stop here, settle, and live quietly in the very place he is desperate to escape. Each is reaching for what the other is trying to leave, and the mayor’s expectations, Lina, and the company’s departure date all press on the little time they have.

Neither of them is free to choose. Puck, the company's aggressive manager, treats Zaira as his property, mistreats her and demands that she stay on the road; the mayor, authoritarian behind a democratic front, orders his son to give up his dreams.

The town’s brief transformation cannot erase its deeper divisions. Joan must choose whether to accept the role assigned to him or break with his family and his town for a life he has glimpsed and may have misread. Their relationship tests the limits of loyalty, class and convention, turning a chance meeting into a painful confrontation between what each of them desires and what their respective worlds will permit.

At its heart, the musical is about the human hunger for freedom, love and a life beyond inherited constraints. It also treats happiness as intensely real yet vulnerable: a passing illumination that can change people forever even when it cannot be held.
